player_0.content: New plan: I incorrectly identified option (A) as sarcastic because I focused on the surface-level irony of "Thank you" paired with distrust, missing the crucial context of the second clause. In option (A), the speaker explicitly states they will *not* trust an unsourced post, which is a logical, albeit cynical, stance, not a sarcastic reversal of meaning. True sarcasm in this context requires saying the opposite of what is meant; option (B) claims the speaker *will* trust an unsourced post over solid advice, which is an illogical, absurd statement intended to mock the idea that unsourced internet opinions hold more weight than expert advice. Next time, I will look for the option that presents an illogical or absurd preference as a genuine statement, as that indicates the speaker is being sarcastic by pretending to value the unsourced opinion. I will select option (B).
